contentBlocks.content: Record Football Without a Dedicated Camera

Professional football camera systems can be valuable, but their hardware, subscriptions and installation are often more than a small-sided team needs. Most amateur players already own the main piece of recording equipment required for Pitchside: a phone with a clear camera and enough battery and storage for the match.

Pitchside is being developed as an AI football camera that begins with a simple, repeatable recording setup. The phone remains stable while the match is played, so a teammate, substitute or coach does not need to follow the ball manually for the entire game.

items: No fixed camera needs to be installed at the venue.
No specialist camera operator is required for the full match.
Teams can begin with one phone and add a second when wider coverage is needed.
The setup can travel between different pitches and venues.
The recording can become the source for highlights and supported match statistics.
Grassroots teams can test the workflow before considering expensive hardware.

contentBlocks.content: Teams that are new to filming should first learn how to record football matches safely and consistently. Good height, framing and stability make more difference than choosing the newest phone and placing it badly.
How the Pitchside Camera App Works

The intended Pitchside workflow connects recording and analysis. Instead of using one application to store video and a separate process to find goals, saves or player moments, the match recording becomes the source for the output produced afterwards.

headers: What Pitchside is being built to do

cells: 1. Set up
Mount one or two phones in a clear and elevated position
Receive footage with enough pitch coverage for analysis
2. Record
Capture the complete small-sided match in landscape orientation
Use the video as the record of what happened
3. Upload
Send the recording through the available beta workflow
Process the footage with a custom small-sided football model
4. Review
Check the returned clips, events and statistics
Turn a long video into useful match and player output

contentBlocks.content: This is why Pitchside is more than a basic football recording app. The aim is not only to save a video file; it is to make the recording useful after full-time by finding supported events and connecting them to teams and players.

Pitchside AI is currently in private beta. The recording, upload and analysis workflow is still improving, and upload and processing can currently take up to 45 minutes depending on the footage and connection.
One-Phone and Two-Phone Recording

One phone can work when it captures the complete small-sided pitch clearly. Two phones are the preferred Pitchside setup because each phone can focus on one half and goal area, helping players remain larger and clearer in the frame.

cells: One phone
Near the halfway line, above head height, with the whole pitch visible where possible
Compact pitches and teams starting with the simplest workflow
Players and goal actions may appear smaller at the far edges
Two phones
Both near halfway, with one phone facing each goal
Larger small-sided pitches and clearer coverage of both halves
Requires two charged phones, two secure mounts and additional setup

contentBlocks.content: Start with one phone if both touchlines and goals remain clear in a short test recording. Move to two phones when players become too small, goalmouth actions lose detail or one camera cannot cover the full playing area without an extremely wide view.

With the two-phone approach, one recording covers each direction of play. Pitchside is being developed to combine the useful data and highlights from both recordings rather than asking users to treat them as two unrelated videos.
Football Camera App Versus Fixed Camera

A fixed football camera system and a phone-based application can both record a match, but they solve the problem in different ways. The best choice depends on budget, venue access, recording frequency and whether the team wants portable footage capture or permanent installed hardware.

contentBlocks.content: Teams comparing dedicated systems with a phone-first workflow can also review the best Veo alternative for football. The right decision is not simply which camera has more features; it is which setup your team can afford, carry, position and use every week.
Turn Footage Into Stats and Highlights

A camera gives you footage. Pitchside is being built to make that footage useful. Its custom computer vision and machine learning model is being developed to identify supported football actions and turn a full recording into match output that players can review.

cells: Goals
Detect goals and assign them to teams and players where supported
Assists
Connect the action before a goal to the assisting player where visible
Saves
Identify goalkeeper saves and important defensive moments
Passes and tackles
Record supported on-ball and defensive contributions
Highlights
Separate useful match and player moments from the full video
Leaderboards
Compare players across supported statistics as match records develop

contentBlocks.content: The AI football highlights page explains the clip experience, while football video analysis covers how the complete recording becomes useful match information. Together, they show why Pitchside is being built as more than a storage camera.

Event detection and player identification are still improving. Camera height, framing, stability, distance, lighting, similar kits and obstructions can all affect what the model can see, so important clips and statistics should be checked during beta.
Best Phone and Mount Setup

The best setup is the one that keeps the phone secure, elevated and pointed at the playing area for the complete match. Pitchside does not require one specific phone model or an expensive branded mount, but the recording must remain clear and stable enough for useful analysis.

items: Use a phone capable of recording a clear, uninterrupted full-match video.
Free sufficient storage before arriving at the pitch.
Charge the phone fully and use an external power source when necessary.
Clean the lens and record in landscape orientation.
Use a stable tripod or mount that can safely raise the phone above head height.
Keep the mount outside the playing area and away from player collisions.
Frame the relevant touchlines and goal before starting the recording.
Record a short test clip and check clarity at the far side of the pitch.
Avoid digital zoom that makes the image unstable or removes pitch coverage.

contentBlocks.content: Use the football recording setup guide for the full one-phone and two-phone positioning process, camera-height guidance and match-day checks. Detailed mount reviews and affiliate comparisons should remain on separate equipment pages rather than this product page.
Supported Match Formats

Pitchside is focused on small-sided football first. Its AI football camera app is being developed around the speed, crowded spaces, camera angles and repeated player actions found in 5-a-side, 6-a-side and 7-a-side matches.

cells: 5-a-side
Core training and development format
One elevated phone may cover a compact pitch; two can improve goal detail
6-a-side
Supported small-sided format
Choose one or two phones according to pitch width and available height
7-a-side
Supported small-sided format
Two phones may offer stronger coverage when one view makes players too distant

contentBlocks.content: Full-size 11-a-side football is not the main focus of the current private beta. Pitchside is deliberately beginning with the grassroots formats its model has been trained to understand, and supported capabilities may change as testing continues.

faqs.question: What is a football camera app?

Yes. One phone can work when it is positioned near halfway, raised above head height and captures the complete small-sided pitch clearly. Two phones can improve coverage when players or goal actions appear too distant.
faqs.question: Can I record a football match with one phone?
Why does Pitchside recommend two phones?
faqs.answer: With two phones, one can face each goal from near the halfway line. This gives clearer coverage of both halves and can keep players and goalmouth actions larger in the recording.
Pitchside does not require one specific phone model. The device should capture clear video, have enough battery and storage for the full match and remain stable in landscape orientation.
faqs.question: Do I need a specific phone to use Pitchside?

faqs.answer: No. The priorities are safety, stability and enough height for a clear view. Use a secure tripod or mount that remains outside the playing area and cannot fall toward players.
faqs.question: Do I need an expensive football camera mount?

faqs.answer: The current private beta focuses on 5-a-side, 6-a-side and 7-a-side football. Full-size 11-a-side is not the main focus of the present small-sided model.
faqs.question: Which match formats does the Pitchside camera app support?
Can Pitchside create highlights from the recording?
faqs.answer: Pitchside is being built to detect supported match events and turn useful moments into highlights. The first-release direction includes goals, assists, saves, passes and tackles.

faqs.question: Can Pitchside produce player statistics?
faqs.answer: Pitchside is being developed to assign supported events and statistics to teams and individual players where the footage allows. Detection and player identification are still improving during beta.

faqs.question: How long does Pitchside take to process a match?
